# Purpose

`weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` ("Long-run income in the interaction") interacts
every deviation term with the unit's long-run climate and its long-run income.
This notebook keeps that model and varies only two things:

- the **deviation definition**: the horizon baseline, the trailing 20 years
  and the trailing 30 years;
- the **form** of each variable's deviation, the same for temperature and
  precipitation, each with one coefficient per arm (no arm has a linear and a
  higher-power term together):

```text
symmetric        dm                              one slope for both signs
linear arms      dT+, dT-
quadratic arms   (dT+)^2, (dT-)^2
cubic arms       (dT+)^3, (dT-)^3
```

The models are fitted on two GDP series (PWT; the World Bank's GDP per capita
at constant 2021 PPP) and three climate datasets (ERA5, CRU TS, UDelaware):
3 definitions x 4 forms x 6 panels = 72 models.

Before that, a check: does the model already estimated (horizon deviations,
linear arms, income = the unit's mean over the horizon) change when income is
the mean of the 20 years before the current year?

Effects are in percentage points (pp) of the annual growth of GDP per capita
for one year at +3 or -3 SD against a year at the unit's trend; `dT+`, `dT-`
(`dP+`, `dP-`) are the positive and negative arms, both positive numbers;
stars are \*\*\* p < 0.01, \*\* p < 0.05, \* p < 0.1.

# Data and specification

The data, the sample, the deviations and the regression are those of
`weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` ("Data and methods"), with the same code; this
notebook repeats only what it needs.

**Data.** GDP per capita from the Penn World Table 11.0 (`rgdpna / pop`,
constant national prices at the 2021 PPP level) and from the World
Development Indicators (`NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD`, constant 2021 international
dollars, October 2026; from 1990, so its growth rates start in 1991). The
outcome is the growth of GDP per capita, the difference of its logarithm
between consecutive calendar years (a gap gives a missing growth rate; nothing
is interpolated, extrapolated or converted). Annual temperature `TM` (°C) and
precipitation `RR` (m) from ERA5, CRU TS or UDelaware in the Weighted Climate
Dataset, with population-density weights at base year 2000. Controls: the
UCDP/PRIO conflict indicators (minor conflict, war) and the post-Soviet and
post-Yugoslav collapse-year dummies.

**Regression.** Year effects, unit effects and unit linear and quadratic
trends (t = year - 1990), as in Burke, Hsiang and Miguel (2015); OLS with the
fixed effects absorbed; errors clustered by country:

```text
g(i,t) = sum over terms a of  dev_a(i,t) x (c_a + b_a clim(i) + h_a inc(i))
         + c1 minor conflict + c2 war + collapse-year dummies
         + unit effect(i) + unit trend(i) x t + unit quadratic trend(i) x t^2 + year effect(t) + error
clim(i) = the unit's mean of the variable over the horizon (°C for T, m a year for P)
inc(i)  = log of the unit's mean GDP per capita over the horizon (every year with
          GDP), minus its mean over the sample rows
```

Income is centred, so `c_a + b_a clim` is the response at the sample's average
income. The long-run climate of the interaction is the horizon mean under
every definition (as the "20-year" definition of the main notebook; not the
"matched" interaction).

**Deviations.** Against the baseline (the horizon: the unit's mean and SD of
the variable from `r params$start_year` to the last year of the panel; or the
mean and SD of the 20 or 30 years before the current one), demeaned (the
unit's mean and linear and quadratic trend removed, fitted on the years from
`r params$start_year` minus ten to the last year, where the baseline exists),
then cut into arms:

```text
dT = (TM - mean) / SD       dm = dT - (unit mean + linear and quadratic trend)
dT+ = max(dm, 0)            dT- = max(-dm, 0)                      (the same for P)
```

**Growth outliers.** The 5% lowest and 5% highest growth rates of PWT x ERA5
from the start year, each annotated with its likely cause; those whose cause
does not involve weather are dropped, from every panel.

**Comparing models.** Where models are compared by AIC, BIC or the within
adjusted R2, the verdict is "indifferent" when the difference cannot be told
apart from noise (clustered Vuong test, or the Wald test of the added terms
for nested models, 5%).

```{r shared-specification}
# As in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd (shared-specification).
START_YEAR <- as.integer(params$start_year)
CLIMATE_WEIGHT <- "population density"
CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR <- 2000L

OUTCOME <- "dlgrp_pc_usd"
# Year effects, unit effects and unit linear and quadratic trends (t = year -
# 1990, t2 = t^2), as in BHM (2015), in every model.
FIXED_EFFECTS <- "year + GID_1[t, t2]"

# The panels keep MAX_LAGS earlier climate years and the demeaning covers them
# (as in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd, so the deviations are the same).
MAX_LAGS <- 10L

# The UCDP/PRIO conflict indicators by the highest intensity of the country's
# conflicts that year (functions/conflict.R): conflict_low, minor (25-999
# battle deaths), and conflict_high, war (1,000 or more); and the post-Soviet
# (with Albania) and post-Yugoslav collapse-year dummies
# (functions/transition_collapse.R).
CONFLICT_TERMS <- c("conflict_low", "conflict_high")
CONTROLS <- c(
  CONFLICT_TERMS,
  "i(fsu_collapse_year, ref = 'none')",
  "i(yug_collapse_year, ref = 'none')"
)

# Growth outliers: the 5% lowest and the 5% highest growth rates of GDP per
# capita of PWT x ERA5 from the start year (found in the panel-builder chunk),
# each with its likely cause, annotated by hand in
# data/growth_outlier_causes.csv and data/growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv;
# every country-year of the tails must have one. Dropped: those whose cause does
# not involve weather (including those with no identified cause), from every
# panel.
OUTLIER_SHARE <- 0.10
OUTLIER_CAUSES <- bind_rows(
  utils::read.csv(data_file("growth_outlier_causes.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  utils::read.csv(data_file("growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(OUTLIER_CAUSES[, c("GID_0", "year")]))

# Moments of the two deviation definitions of the main notebook: over the
# horizon of the panel (*_all, replaced below) and over the 20 years before the
# current one. The sample of the main notebook requires both; the 30-year
# moments are required on top of them in the sensitivity (SENS_MOMENTS).
MOMENTS <- c(
  "mean_TM_all", "sd_TM_all", "mean_RR_all", "sd_RR_all",
  "mean_TM_lag_20", "sd_TM_lag_20", "mean_RR_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20"
)
# The demeaned deviations of each variable and baseline (built by
# prepare_panel()); the sample of the main notebook requires those of the
# horizon and 20-year baselines.
BASELINES <- c("all", "lag_20", "lag_30")
DEMEANED <- as.vector(outer(c("TM", "RR"), c("all", "lag_20"), function(v, b) paste0("dm_", v, "_", b)))

fit_model <- function(terms, model_data, fixed_effects = FIXED_EFFECTS, outcome = OUTCOME) {
  m <- fit_panel_model(
    paste(terms, collapse = " + "),
    model_data,
    outcome = outcome,
    fixed_effects = fixed_effects,
    cluster = ~GID_0
  )
  # The country of each estimation row, for the noise tests of differences in fit.
  m$country <- model_data$GID_0[fixest::obs(m)]
  m
}

# Labels for the coefficient tables; the collapse dummies are left out of them.
DICT <- c(
  conflict_low = "Conflict, minor", conflict_high = "Conflict, war",
  clim_TM = "mean T", clim_RR = "mean P", inc = "income",
  devTM = "dT", devTM_pos = "dT+", devTM_neg = "dT-",
  devTM_pos2 = "(dT+)^2", devTM_neg2 = "(dT-)^2", devTM_pos3 = "(dT+)^3", devTM_neg3 = "(dT-)^3",
  devRR = "dP", devRR_pos = "dP+", devRR_neg = "dP-",
  devRR_pos2 = "(dP+)^2", devRR_neg2 = "(dP-)^2", devRR_pos3 = "(dP+)^3", devRR_neg3 = "(dP-)^3"
)
DROP <- "collapse_year"
# Temperature terms, then precipitation terms, then the controls (original names).
ORDER <- c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^conflict")
FITSTAT <- ~n + wr2 + aic + bic
```

The panels: PWT and World Bank PPP, each with ERA5, CRU TS and UDelaware. The
sample is the unit-years with growth, both weather variables, the conflict
indicators and the moments of the horizon and 20-year deviations (positive
SDs), without the non-weather growth outliers: the sample of the main
notebook. For the World Bank PPP panels the horizon of the climate baseline is
the same as PWT's (`r params$start_year` to the last year), so a country-year
has the same deviation in both; their rows start in 1991.

```{r panel-builder}
# As in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd (panel-builder), with the demeaned 30-year
# deviations added (BASELINES).
# Panel `econ` x `source` from `start_year`, with the horizon moments, the
# controls, the sample with and without the country-years `drop`, the rows
# dropped, and every unit-year of the panel (`data`).
prepare_panel <- function(econ, source, econ_variable = NULL, drop = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
                          start_year = START_YEAR) {
  cfg <- panel_config(
    econ_year_min = start_year,
    climate_source = source,
    climate_weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT,
    climate_weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
    # Eleven earlier climate years: up to ten carry the lags of the deviations
    # into the first years, one the lagged trailing moments. The sample starts
    # at start_year regardless.
    clim_history_years = 11L
  )
  data <- suppressMessages(build_dat(econ_data = econ, config = cfg,
                                     econ_variable = econ_variable))
  level <- unique(data$gadm_level)
  end_year <- max(data$year[est_row(data) & !is.na(data$TM) & !is.na(data$RR)])

  horizon <- load_climate_panel(level, cfg) %>%
    filter(gadm_level == level, year >= start_year, year <= end_year) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_TM_all = mean(TM, na.rm = TRUE), sd_TM_all = sd(TM, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_RR_all = mean(RR, na.rm = TRUE), sd_RR_all = sd(RR, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  data <- data %>%
    select(-c(mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all)) %>%
    left_join(horizon, by = "GID_1")
  data <- add_yugoslav_collapse(add_soviet_collapse(add_conflict(data)))
  data$t <- data$year - 1990L
  data$t2 <- data$t^2

  # Demeaned deviations: each unit's mean and quadratic trend removed.
  window <- data$year >= start_year - MAX_LAGS & data$year <= end_year
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (b in BASELINES) {
    raw <- (data[[v]] - data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", b)]]) / data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", b)]]
    ok <- which(window & is.finite(raw))
    sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = data$GID_1[ok], t = data$t[ok], t2 = data$t2[ok], x = raw[ok])
    m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
    demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
    demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
    data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", b)]] <- demeaned
  }

  complete <- stats::complete.cases(
    as.data.frame(data)[, c(OUTCOME, "TM", "RR", CONFLICT_TERMS, MOMENTS, DEMEANED)]
  )
  positive_sd <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(grep("^sd_", MOMENTS, value = TRUE), function(x) {
    !is.na(data[[x]]) & data[[x]] > 0
  }))
  sample_all <- data[est_row(data) & data$year >= start_year & complete & positive_sd, ]
  apply_exclusions(list(
    label = paste(sub("_", " ", econ), "x", source), econ = econ, source = source, level = level,
    start_year = start_year, end_year = end_year, all = sample_all, data = data
  ), drop)
}

# The sample of panel `p` without the country-years `drop` (clean), and the
# rows dropped (outliers).
apply_exclusions <- function(p, drop) {
  dropped <- paste(p$all$GID_0, p$all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  p$clean <- p$all[!dropped, ]
  p$outliers <- p$all[dropped, c("GID_0", "GID_1", "year", OUTCOME)]
  p
}

# The outliers are the growth tails of the main panel (PWT x ERA5) from the
# start year, so it is built first, without exclusions. Every country-year of
# the tails must have an annotated cause.
main <- prepare_panel("PWT", "ERA5", drop = OUTLIER_CAUSES[0, c("GID_0", "year")])
cutoffs <- stats::quantile(main$all[[OUTCOME]], c(OUTLIER_SHARE / 2, 1 - OUTLIER_SHARE / 2),
                           names = FALSE)
tails <- main$all[main$all[[OUTCOME]] < cutoffs[[1]] | main$all[[OUTCOME]] > cutoffs[[2]], ]
country_year <- function(d) paste(d$GID_0, d$year)
stopifnot(all(country_year(tails) %in% country_year(OUTLIER_CAUSES)))
OUTLIERS <- OUTLIER_CAUSES[country_year(OUTLIER_CAUSES) %in% country_year(tails), ]
OUTLIERS_DROPPED <- OUTLIERS[OUTLIERS$weather == "no", c("GID_0", "year")]
main <- apply_exclusions(main, OUTLIERS_DROPPED)

# The panels of the sensitivity: PWT and World Bank PPP with each climate dataset.
SENS_GRID <- expand.grid(source = c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"), econ = c("PWT", "WB_PPP"),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sens_panels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(SENS_GRID)), function(i) {
  if (SENS_GRID$econ[i] == "PWT" && SENS_GRID$source[i] == "ERA5") return(main)
  prepare_panel(SENS_GRID$econ[i], SENS_GRID$source[i])
})
names(sens_panels) <- vapply(sens_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
stopifnot(names(sens_panels)[[1]] == "PWT x ERA5")
```

```{r model-helpers}
# As in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd (model-helpers and income-interaction),
# with cubic arms added.
# Deviation terms of the demeaned deviations dm_<v>_<suffix>, with one suffix
# per variable (a definition), and the long-run climate they are interacted
# with, clim_<v> = mean_<v>_<suffix[["clim_<v>"]]>.
add_deviation_terms <- function(model_data, suffix) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    dev <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]] <- dev
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)^2
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)^2
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos3")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)^3
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg3")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)^3
    clim <- paste0("clim_", v)
    model_data[[clim]] <- model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", suffix[[clim]])]]
  }
  model_data
}
definition <- function(TM, RR, matched = FALSE) {
  c(TM = TM, RR = RR, clim_TM = if (matched) TM else "all", clim_RR = if (matched) RR else "all")
}
DEFINITIONS <- list(
  "Horizon" = definition("all", "all"),
  "20-year" = definition("lag_20", "lag_20"),
  "30-year" = definition("lag_30", "lag_30")
)
# Each form: the deviation terms of each variable, by column suffix; one term
# per arm.
FORMS <- list(
  "Symmetric" = list(TM = "", RR = ""),
  "Linear arms" = list(TM = c("_pos", "_neg"), RR = c("_pos", "_neg")),
  "Quadratic arms" = list(TM = c("_pos2", "_neg2"), RR = c("_pos2", "_neg2")),
  "Cubic arms" = list(TM = c("_pos3", "_neg3"), RR = c("_pos3", "_neg3"))
)

form_terms <- function(form) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    x <- paste0("dev", v, form[[v]])
    c(x, paste0(x, ":clim_", v))
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}
# Every deviation term of `form` interacted with income.
income_interactions <- function(form) {
  unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) paste0("dev", v, form[[v]], ":inc")))
}
# Value of a deviation term (by column suffix) at deviations x.
term_value <- function(suffix, x) {
  if (suffix == "") return(x)
  switch(suffix, "_pos" = pmax(x, 0), "_neg" = pmax(-x, 0),
         "_pos2" = pmax(x, 0)^2, "_neg2" = pmax(-x, 0)^2,
         "_pos3" = pmax(x, 0)^3, "_neg3" = pmax(-x, 0)^3)
}
interaction_name <- function(a, b, terms) {
  intersect(c(paste0(a, ":", b), paste0(b, ":", a)), terms)[[1]]
}
wald_p <- function(m, pattern) fixest::wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p
stars <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.01, "***", ifelse(p < 0.05, "**", ifelse(p < 0.1, "*", "")))
# Patterns of the joint tests: every deviation term of variable v (with its
# interactions), its interactions with income, its interactions with the
# long-run climate.
dev_pattern <- function(v) paste0("^dev", v)
income_pattern <- function(v) paste0("^dev", v, ".*:inc$|^inc:dev", v)
climate_pattern <- function(v) paste0("clim_", v)

# Differences in fit against noise (see weather_arms_robustness.Rmd): a Vuong
# test clustered by country for non-nested models, the clustered Wald test of
# the added terms for nested ones; "indifferent" when not beyond noise at 5%.
NOISE_LEVEL <- 0.05
CRITERIA <- c(aic = "AIC", bic = "BIC", r2 = "within adj. R2")
fit_record <- function(m) {
  e <- stats::resid(m)
  s2 <- mean(e^2)
  list(aic = stats::AIC(m), bic = stats::BIC(m), war2 = fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]],
       n = stats::nobs(m), ll = -0.5 * log(2 * pi * s2) - e^2 / (2 * s2), country = m$country)
}
as_record <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "fixest")) fit_record(x) else x
criterion_value <- function(rec, criterion) {
  switch(criterion, aic = -rec$aic / 2, bic = -rec$bic / 2, r2 = -(rec$n / 2) * log(1 - rec$war2))
}
fit_verdict <- function(a, b, criterion, nested_p = NULL) {
  a <- as_record(a)
  b <- as_record(b)
  stopifnot(a$n == b$n, identical(a$country, b$country))
  difference <- criterion_value(a, criterion) - criterion_value(b, criterion)
  beyond_noise <- if (!is.null(nested_p)) {
    !is.na(nested_p) && nested_p < NOISE_LEVEL
  } else {
    D <- tapply(a$ll - b$ll, a$country, sum)
    G <- length(D)
    se <- sqrt(G / (G - 1) * sum((D - mean(D))^2))
    is.finite(se) && se > 0 && abs(difference / se) >= stats::qnorm(1 - NOISE_LEVEL / 2)
  }
  if (!beyond_noise) "indifferent" else if (difference > 0) "better" else "worse"
}
fit_verdicts <- function(a, b, nested_p = NULL) {
  a <- as_record(a)
  b <- as_record(b)
  paste(vapply(names(CRITERIA), function(cr) fit_verdict(a, b, cr, nested_p), ""),
        collapse = " / ")
}
# Each model of a set (records on the same rows) against the best of the set
# by `criterion`: "best", "indifferent" or "worse".
verdicts_vs_best <- function(records, criterion) {
  records <- lapply(records, as_record)
  value <- vapply(records, criterion_value, 0, criterion)
  best <- which.max(value)
  vapply(seq_along(records), function(i) {
    if (i == best) "best" else fit_verdict(records[[i]], records[[best]], criterion)
  }, "")
}
# The three verdicts of each model of a set against the best, "AIC / BIC / R2".
set_verdicts <- function(records) {
  verdicts <- lapply(names(CRITERIA), function(cr) verdicts_vs_best(records, cr))
  do.call(paste, c(verdicts, sep = " / "))
}
added_terms_p <- function(larger, smaller) {
  added <- setdiff(names(stats::coef(larger)), names(stats::coef(smaller)))
  stopifnot(length(added) > 0, all(names(stats::coef(smaller)) %in% names(stats::coef(larger))))
  b <- stats::coef(larger)[added]
  V <- stats::vcov(larger)[added, added, drop = FALSE]
  stats::pchisq(as.numeric(t(b) %*% solve(V, b)), df = length(added), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
VERDICT_NOTE <- paste(
  "verdict by AIC / BIC / within adjusted R2: indifferent when the difference cannot be told",
  "apart from noise (clustered Vuong test, or the Wald test of the added terms for nested",
  "models, 5%)")

# Deviations (SD) and long-run climates (C, m a year) at which the effects are
# evaluated.
EFFECT_AT <- c(-3, 3)
EVAL_CLIMATE <- list(TM = c(5, 15, 25), RR = c(0.5, 1.5, 3))
EVAL_LABELS <- list(TM = c("5 °C", "15 °C", "25 °C"), RR = c("0.5 m", "1.5 m", "3 m"))

# Each unit's long-run income over the horizon of panel `p`, centred at the mean
# over the rows `d`.
add_income <- function(p, d) {
  income <- p$data %>%
    filter(year >= p$start_year, year <= p$end_year, !is.na(grp_pc_usd)) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(inc_level = log(mean(grp_pc_usd)), .groups = "drop")
  d <- left_join(d, income, by = "GID_1")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$inc_level))
  d$inc <- d$inc_level - mean(d$inc_level)
  d
}
# Weights on the coefficients `terms` of a deviation x (SD) of variable v in a
# model with the terms `suffixes`, at the values `modifiers` (named: the
# variables interacted with every deviation term, e.g. clim_TM, inc).
deviation_weights <- function(terms, suffixes, v, x, modifiers) {
  w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
  for (s in suffixes) {
    term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
    w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
    for (z in names(modifiers)) {
      w[[interaction_name(term, z, terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * modifiers[[z]]
    }
  }
  w
}
# Effects (pp, 95% CI) of EFFECT_AT SD of each variable at each long-run
# climate of EVAL_CLIMATE in model m (terms `form`), at the extra modifiers
# `at` (e.g. list(inc = 0)).
effects_at <- function(m, form, at = list()) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]), deviation = EFFECT_AT)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
      mods <- c(stats::setNames(list(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]][[g]]), paste0("clim_", v)), at)
      deviation_weights(terms, form[[v]], v, x, mods)
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(m, G) %>%
      mutate(variable = v, level = EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}
effect_cell <- function(e) {
  sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", 100 * e$estimate, 100 * e$conf_low, 100 * e$conf_high,
          stars(e$p_value))
}
effect_column <- function(e) paste0(ifelse(e$variable == "TM", "T ", "P "),
                                    sprintf("%+d SD, ", e$deviation), e$level)
```

# Check: income over the previous 20 years

The model already estimated in `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` (horizon
deviations, linear arms for T and P, on `r main$label`) interacts the arms with
one income per unit, the mean over the whole horizon. That income includes the
years after the current one, and it is fixed. The alternative is the income of
the 20 years before the current year:

```text
inc20(i,t) = log of the mean GDP per capita of unit i over t-20 .. t-1, minus its mean over the rows
```

It is built from the same GDP series as the outcome (PWT, from 1950). It is
defined only when all 20 years have GDP: no partial windows, nothing filled.
For example, a country whose PWT series starts in 1970 has it from 1990. Unlike
the horizon income, it varies within a unit, so the unit effects no longer
absorb its level. The model therefore has it in two versions, with its level
(`inc`, mostly mean reversion within units, as in "Preferred model and lagged
income" of the main notebook) and without. The models:

```text
A  horizon income, all the rows of the main notebook (the model already estimated)
B  horizon income, on the rows with inc20 (re-centred on them)
C  inc20 in the interactions, and its level
D  inc20 in the interactions, without its level
```

B, C and D are on the same rows, so the effect of the income definition is
C (or D) against B, and the effect of the rows is B against A. The tables:

1. the rows, and how the two incomes relate;
2. the coefficients;
3. the joint tests and the verdicts against B;
4. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate. They are evaluated
   at the same levels of GDP per capita in every model: the geometric mean of
   the rows of B, C and D, and the mean log income (horizon) of the poorest and
   of the richest third of the units of A. Each level is converted to each
   model's own centring.

```{r income-window-check}
INCOME_WINDOW <- 20L
CHECK_FORM <- FORMS[["Linear arms"]]
# Each unit-year's log of the mean GDP per capita of the `window` years before
# it (t - window .. t - 1), from GDP series `econ` over every year of the source;
# NA unless all of those years have GDP (no partial windows, nothing filled).
trailing_income <- function(econ, window = INCOME_WINDOW) {
  stored <- resolve_econ_source(econ)
  load_econ_panel(stored) %>%
    filter(gadm_level == GADM_LEVEL_BY_SOURCE[[stored]]) %>%
    distinct(GID_1, year, grp_pc_usd) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    tidyr::complete(year = seq(min(year), max(year))) %>%
    arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(window_mean = zoo::rollapplyr(grp_pc_usd, window, mean, fill = NA_real_),
           inc_trailing_level = log(lag_by_year(window_mean, year))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(GID_1, year, inc_trailing_level)
}
inc20 <- trailing_income("PWT")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(inc20[, c("GID_1", "year")]))

check_all <- add_income(main, add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]])) %>%
  left_join(inc20, by = c("GID_1", "year"))
check_rows <- check_all[is.finite(check_all$inc_trailing_level), ]
# B: the horizon income, re-centred on these rows; C, D: the trailing income.
horizon_rows <- mutate(check_rows, inc = inc_level - mean(inc_level))
trailing_rows <- mutate(check_rows, inc = inc_trailing_level - mean(inc_trailing_level))
check_terms <- c(form_terms(CHECK_FORM), income_interactions(CHECK_FORM))
check_models <- list(
  "A. horizon income, all rows" = fit_model(check_terms, check_all),
  "B. horizon income, inc20 rows" = fit_model(check_terms, horizon_rows),
  "C. inc20, with its level" = fit_model(c(check_terms, "inc"), trailing_rows),
  "D. inc20, without its level" = fit_model(check_terms, trailing_rows)
)
# The centre of each model's income, to evaluate them at the same GDP per capita.
check_centres <- c(mean(check_all$inc_level), mean(check_rows$inc_level),
                   mean(check_rows$inc_trailing_level), mean(check_rows$inc_trailing_level))
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(check_models[-1], stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)

# 1. The rows and the two incomes.
within_sd <- check_rows %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  summarise(sd = stats::sd(inc_trailing_level), .groups = "drop")
tibble::tibble(
  rows = c("all rows of the main notebook (A)", "rows with inc20 (B, C, D)"),
  observations = c(nrow(check_all), nrow(check_rows)),
  countries = c(n_distinct(check_all$GID_0), n_distinct(check_rows$GID_0)),
  years = c(paste(range(check_all$year), collapse = "-"), paste(range(check_rows$year), collapse = "-")),
  mean_log_income_horizon = round(c(mean(check_all$inc_level), mean(check_rows$inc_level)), 2),
  mean_log_income_inc20 = c(NA, round(mean(check_rows$inc_trailing_level), 2))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, the rows of the check; on the rows with inc20: correlation of the horizon log income",
    "with inc20 %.3f; SD of inc20 across the rows %.2f, within units (mean of the units' SDs)",
    "%.2f; mean of horizon minus inc20 %.2f log points"),
    main$label, stats::cor(check_rows$inc_level, check_rows$inc_trailing_level),
    stats::sd(check_rows$inc_trailing_level), mean(within_sd$sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(check_rows$inc_level - check_rows$inc_trailing_level)))

# 2. Coefficients.
etable(unname(check_models), headers = names(check_models), dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c(ORDER, "^income$"), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = paste0(main$label, ", linear arms, horizon deviations"))

# 3. Joint tests, and the verdicts against B (same rows; C against D: nested,
# the Wald test of the level).
check_tests <- function(m) {
  c(income_T = wald_p(m, income_pattern("TM")), income_P = wald_p(m, income_pattern("RR")),
    climate_T = wald_p(m, climate_pattern("TM")), climate_P = wald_p(m, climate_pattern("RR")),
    T = wald_p(m, dev_pattern("TM")), P = wald_p(m, dev_pattern("RR")))
}
level_p <- added_terms_p(check_models[[3]], check_models[[4]])
bind_rows(lapply(names(check_models), function(k) {
  m <- check_models[[k]]
  tibble::as_tibble(as.list(signif(check_tests(m), 2))) %>%
    mutate(model = k, observations = stats::nobs(m),
           within_adj_r2 = round(fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 5),
           income_level = if ("inc" %in% names(stats::coef(m))) {
             sprintf("%.4f (%.4f)", stats::coef(m)[["inc"]], fixest::se(m)[["inc"]])
           } else "",
           against_B = if (k %in% names(check_models)[3:4]) {
             fit_verdicts(m, check_models[[2]])
           } else "",
           .before = 1)
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": joint Wald tests (p) of each variable's income interactions, climate ",
    "interactions and all its deviation terms; the coefficient (SE) of the level of inc20; ",
    "C and D against B, ", VERDICT_NOTE, ". C against D (nested, the level): p = ",
    signif(level_p, 2), ", ", fit_verdicts(check_models[[3]], check_models[[4]], nested_p = level_p)))

# 4. Effects at the same GDP per capita levels.
unit_income <- distinct(check_all, GID_1, inc_level)
third <- dplyr::ntile(unit_income$inc_level, 3)
CHECK_INCOME <- c("geometric mean of the inc20 rows" = mean(check_rows$inc_level),
                  "poorest third" = mean(unit_income$inc_level[third == 1]),
                  "richest third" = mean(unit_income$inc_level[third == 3]))
check_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(check_models), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(CHECK_INCOME), function(lvl) {
    effects_at(check_models[[i]], CHECK_FORM, list(inc = CHECK_INCOME[[lvl]] - check_centres[[i]])) %>%
      mutate(model = names(check_models)[[i]], income = lvl)
  }))
}))
for (lvl in names(CHECK_INCOME)) {
  e <- filter(check_effects, income == lvl)
  print(knitr::kable(
    e %>%
      mutate(column = factor(effect_column(e), levels = unique(effect_column(e))),
             cell = effect_cell(e)) %>%
      select(column, model, cell) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell),
    caption = sprintf(paste(
      "%s: effect (pp, 95%% CI) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate, at the %s income",
      "(GDP per capita %s); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"),
      main$label, lvl, format(round(exp(CHECK_INCOME[[lvl]])), big.mark = ","))))
}
```

Model A (horizon deviations, linear arms, horizon climate and income, on every
row of the main notebook) is saved for later use, as the models of
`results/preferred_model/`. The files are its weather coefficients with their
VCOV (clustered by country), and the values that are needed to apply them: the
centre of income and the number of rows and countries.

```{r income-model-export}
local({
  m <- check_models[["A. horizon income, all rows"]]
  weather <- grep("^dev(TM|RR)|^inc:dev", names(stats::coef(m)), value = TRUE)
  stem <- file.path("results", "preferred_model", "pwt_era5_horizon_linear_arms_income")
  dir.create(dirname(stem), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)[weather, , drop = FALSE]
  utils::write.csv(tibble::tibble(
    term = weather, estimate = ct[, 1], std_error = ct[, 2],
    conf_low_95 = ct[, 1] - stats::qnorm(0.975) * ct[, 2],
    conf_high_95 = ct[, 1] + stats::qnorm(0.975) * ct[, 2],
    p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(ct[, 1] / ct[, 2]))
  ), paste0(stem, "_coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  V <- stats::vcov(m)[weather, weather]
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(term = weather, V, check.names = FALSE),
                   paste0(stem, "_vcov.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(tibble::tibble(
    item = c("panel", "deviations", "form", "climate_interaction", "income",
             "income_centre_log_gdp_pc", "observations", "countries", "years", "vcov"),
    value = c(main$label, "horizon, demeaned", "linear arms (T and P)",
              "horizon mean of TM (C) and RR (m a year)",
              "log of the unit's mean GDP per capita over the horizon, minus income_centre_log_gdp_pc",
              format(mean(check_all$inc_level), digits = 10), stats::nobs(m),
              n_distinct(check_all$GID_0), paste(range(check_all$year), collapse = "-"),
              "clustered by country (GID_0)")
  ), paste0(stem, "_info.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
})
```

The same model with restricted cubic splines in both the climate and income
interactions is saved too. It is refitted here as in "Splines in climate and
income" of the main notebook. Each interaction is the variable itself plus two
non-linear terms, with knots at the 5th, 35th, 65th and 95th percentiles of the
units. The spline is linear beyond the outer knots:

```text
slope of arm a = c_a + b_a clim + d_a1 nl_1(clim) + d_a2 nl_2(clim) + h_a inc + g_a1 nl_1(inc) + g_a2 nl_2(inc)
nl_j(x) = [ (x - k_j)^3_+ - (x - k_3)^3_+ (k_4 - k_j) / (k_4 - k_3)
            + (x - k_4)^3_+ (k_3 - k_j) / (k_4 - k_3) ] / (k_4 - k_1)^2          j = 1, 2
```

The knots of income are on the centred scale (`inc`); the knots file also gives
them as log GDP per capita and as GDP per capita.

```{r spline-model-export}
SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS <- c(0.05, 0.35, 0.65, 0.95)
# Restricted cubic spline basis of x with `knots` (Harrell): the K - 2
# non-linear terms, scaled by the squared range of the knots (as in
# weather_arms_robustness.Rmd).
rcs_nonlinear <- function(x, knots) {
  K <- length(knots)
  cube <- function(z) pmax(z, 0)^3
  out <- vapply(seq_len(K - 2), function(j) {
    (cube(x - knots[[j]]) -
       cube(x - knots[[K - 1]]) * (knots[[K]] - knots[[j]]) / (knots[[K]] - knots[[K - 1]]) +
       cube(x - knots[[K]]) * (knots[[K - 1]] - knots[[j]]) / (knots[[K]] - knots[[K - 1]])) /
      (knots[[K]] - knots[[1]])^2
  }, numeric(length(x)))
  matrix(out, nrow = length(x))
}
spline_units <- distinct(check_all, GID_1, inc, clim_TM, clim_RR)
spline_knots <- lapply(c(clim_TM = "clim_TM", clim_RR = "clim_RR", inc = "inc"), function(z) {
  stats::quantile(spline_units[[z]], SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE)
})
spline_data <- check_all
for (z in names(spline_knots)) {
  nl <- rcs_nonlinear(spline_data[[z]], spline_knots[[z]])
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(nl))) spline_data[[paste0(z, "_nl", j)]] <- nl[, j]
}
spline_terms <- c(check_terms, unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  arms <- paste0("dev", v, CHECK_FORM[[v]])
  as.vector(outer(arms, c(paste0(":clim_", v, "_nl", 1:2), paste0(":inc_nl", 1:2)), paste0))
})))
spline_model <- fit_model(spline_terms, spline_data)
linear_model <- check_models[["A. horizon income, all rows"]]
stopifnot(stats::nobs(spline_model) == stats::nobs(linear_model))
spline_p <- added_terms_p(spline_model, linear_model)

tibble::tibble(
  model = c("linear interactions", "splines in climate and income"),
  observations = c(stats::nobs(linear_model), stats::nobs(spline_model)),
  within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * c(fixest::fitstat(linear_model, "war2")[[1]],
                                    fixest::fitstat(spline_model, "war2")[[1]]), 3),
  aic_vs_linear = round(c(0, stats::AIC(spline_model) - stats::AIC(linear_model)), 1),
  bic_vs_linear = round(c(0, stats::BIC(spline_model) - stats::BIC(linear_model)), 1),
  verdict_vs_linear = c("", fit_verdicts(spline_model, linear_model, nested_p = spline_p))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", linear arms, horizon deviations: the splines against the linear interactions ",
    "(nested: the Wald test of the non-linear terms, p = ", signif(spline_p, 2), "); ", VERDICT_NOTE))

# Saves spline model m, fitted on the rows `d` with the knots `knots`, as
# <stem>_coefficients.csv, _vcov.csv, _knots.csv and _info.csv; `outliers`
# describes the growth outliers dropped.
export_spline_model <- function(m, d, knots, stem, outliers) {
  weather <- grep("^dev(TM|RR)|^(inc|clim_)[^:]*:dev", names(stats::coef(m)), value = TRUE)
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)[weather, , drop = FALSE]
  utils::write.csv(tibble::tibble(
    term = weather, estimate = ct[, 1], std_error = ct[, 2],
    conf_low_95 = ct[, 1] - stats::qnorm(0.975) * ct[, 2],
    conf_high_95 = ct[, 1] + stats::qnorm(0.975) * ct[, 2],
    p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(ct[, 1] / ct[, 2]))
  ), paste0(stem, "_coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(term = weather, stats::vcov(m)[weather, weather], check.names = FALSE),
                   paste0(stem, "_vcov.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  centre <- mean(d$inc_level)
  knot_table <- tibble::tibble(
    variable = c("clim_TM", "clim_RR", "inc", "inc", "inc"),
    scale = c("long-run temperature (C)", "long-run precipitation (m a year)",
              "inc: centred log GDP per capita (as in the model)", "log GDP per capita",
              "GDP per capita (2021 PPP $)"),
    knot_1 = NA_real_, knot_2 = NA_real_, knot_3 = NA_real_, knot_4 = NA_real_
  )
  knot_table[, paste0("knot_", 1:4)] <- rbind(knots$clim_TM, knots$clim_RR, knots$inc,
                                              knots$inc + centre, exp(knots$inc + centre))
  utils::write.csv(knot_table, paste0(stem, "_knots.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(tibble::tibble(
    item = c("panel", "deviations", "form", "interactions", "basis", "knots", "income",
             "income_centre_log_gdp_pc", "observations", "countries", "years", "growth_outliers",
             "vcov"),
    value = c(main$label, "horizon, demeaned", "linear arms (T and P)",
              paste("each arm x (clim, clim_nl1, clim_nl2, inc, inc_nl1, inc_nl2); clim: horizon mean",
                    "of TM (C) or RR (m a year)"),
              paste("restricted cubic spline (Harrell): nl_j(x) = [(x-k_j)^3_+ - (x-k_3)^3_+ (k_4-k_j)/(k_4-k_3)",
                    "+ (x-k_4)^3_+ (k_3-k_j)/(k_4-k_3)] / (k_4-k_1)^2, j = 1, 2; linear beyond k_1 and k_4"),
              "5th, 35th, 65th and 95th percentiles of the units (see _knots.csv)",
              "log of the unit's mean GDP per capita over the horizon, minus income_centre_log_gdp_pc",
              format(centre, digits = 10), stats::nobs(m), n_distinct(d$GID_0),
              paste(range(d$year), collapse = "-"), outliers, "clustered by country (GID_0)")
  ), paste0(stem, "_info.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
SPLINE_STEM <- file.path("results", "preferred_model", "pwt_era5_horizon_linear_arms_income_climate_splines")
export_spline_model(spline_model, check_all, spline_knots, SPLINE_STEM, paste(
  "the 5% lowest and 5% highest growth rates of PWT x ERA5 from the start year whose cause",
  "does not involve weather dropped"))
```

## Splines with only the 1% tails dropped

The spline model above drops the growth outliers of the main rule: the 5%
lowest and 5% highest growth rates, those whose cause does not involve
weather. Here the tails are the 1% lowest and the 1% highest growth rates of
`r main$label` from the start year, found in the same way (before any
exclusion). Two samples:

- **1% tails dropped**: every country-year of the two tails is dropped,
  whatever its cause;
- **1% tails, non-weather dropped**: the cause rule of the main sample applied
  to the 1% tails (the weather-related ones stay).

Everything else is as above, and the knots and the centre of income are
recomputed on each sample. A coefficient therefore means something slightly
different in each sample, so the samples are compared by their effects at
fixed values. The effects are those of a +/-3 SD year for a typical unit of
each third of income: the geometric mean income and the mean long-run climate
of the third's units in the main sample. The tables:

1. the samples: the rows, the dropped country-years by cause, and the fit
   against the linear interactions on the same rows;
2. the effects in each sample;
3. figure: the effects across income at the main sample's average climate.

The model of the first sample is saved as
`results/preferred_model/pwt_era5_horizon_linear_arms_income_climate_splines_tails1pct_*.csv`,
in the same format.

```{r spline-tails-1pct, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7}
TAIL_SHARE <- 0.01
# The spline model with the linear interactions on the rows `d` (with
# inc_level): the knots and the income centre of the rows.
fit_splines <- function(d) {
  d$inc <- d$inc_level - mean(d$inc_level)
  units <- distinct(d, GID_1, inc, clim_TM, clim_RR)
  knots <- lapply(c(clim_TM = "clim_TM", clim_RR = "clim_RR", inc = "inc"), function(z) {
    stats::quantile(units[[z]], SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE)
  })
  for (z in names(knots)) {
    nl <- rcs_nonlinear(d[[z]], knots[[z]])
    for (j in seq_len(ncol(nl))) d[[paste0(z, "_nl", j)]] <- nl[, j]
  }
  list(spline = fit_model(spline_terms, d), linear = fit_model(check_terms, d), d = d,
       knots = knots, centre = mean(d$inc_level))
}
# Effects (linear_combination) of a deviation x of variable v in spline fit `f`
# at long-run climates `clim` and log GDP per capita `level` (vectors).
spline_effect <- function(f, v, x, clim, level) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(f$spline))
  clim_name <- paste0("clim_", v)
  G <- t(vapply(seq_along(clim), function(i) {
    inc <- level[[i]] - f$centre
    nl_clim <- rcs_nonlinear(clim[[i]], f$knots[[clim_name]])
    nl_inc <- rcs_nonlinear(inc, f$knots$inc)
    mods <- c(stats::setNames(list(clim[[i]], nl_clim[1, 1], nl_clim[1, 2]),
                              paste0(clim_name, c("", "_nl1", "_nl2"))),
              list(inc = inc, inc_nl1 = nl_inc[1, 1], inc_nl2 = nl_inc[1, 2]))
    deviation_weights(terms, CHECK_FORM[[v]], v, x, mods)
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(f$spline, G)
}

cutoffs_1pct <- stats::quantile(main$all[[OUTCOME]], c(TAIL_SHARE, 1 - TAIL_SHARE), names = FALSE)
tails_1pct <- main$all[main$all[[OUTCOME]] < cutoffs_1pct[[1]] |
                         main$all[[OUTCOME]] > cutoffs_1pct[[2]], ]
# The 1% tails are inside the 5% tails, so each has an annotated cause.
stopifnot(all(country_year(tails_1pct) %in% country_year(OUTLIERS)))
tails_1pct <- OUTLIERS[country_year(OUTLIERS) %in% country_year(tails_1pct), ]
TAIL_SAMPLES <- list(
  "main rule (5% tails, non-weather dropped)" = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
  "1% tails dropped" = tails_1pct[, c("GID_0", "year")],
  "1% tails, non-weather dropped" = tails_1pct[tails_1pct$weather == "no", c("GID_0", "year")]
)
main_rows <- add_income(main, add_deviation_terms(main$all, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]]))
tail_fits <- lapply(TAIL_SAMPLES, function(drop) {
  fit_splines(main_rows[!country_year(main_rows) %in% country_year(drop), ])
})
# The main rule reproduces the spline model above.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(stats::AIC(tail_fits[[1]]$spline), stats::AIC(spline_model))))

# 1. The samples.
tibble::tibble(
  sample = names(TAIL_SAMPLES),
  dropped = vapply(TAIL_SAMPLES, nrow, 0),
  observations = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) stats::nobs(f$spline), 0),
  within_adj_r2_pct = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) round(100 * fixest::fitstat(f$spline, "war2")[[1]], 3), 0),
  linear_within_adj_r2_pct = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) round(100 * fixest::fitstat(f$linear, "war2")[[1]], 3), 0),
  aic_vs_linear = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) round(stats::AIC(f$spline) - stats::AIC(f$linear), 1), 0),
  bic_vs_linear = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) round(stats::BIC(f$spline) - stats::BIC(f$linear), 1), 0),
  nonlinear_p = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) signif(added_terms_p(f$spline, f$linear), 2), 0),
  verdict_vs_linear = vapply(tail_fits, function(f) {
    fit_verdicts(f$spline, f$linear, nested_p = added_terms_p(f$spline, f$linear))
  }, "")
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, splines in climate and income: the country-years dropped, the rows, the within adjusted",
    "R2 (%%) of the splines and of the linear interactions, and the splines against the linear",
    "interactions on the same rows (nested: the Wald test of the non-linear terms); %s. The 1%%",
    "tails: growth below %.1f%% or above %.1f%%"),
    main$label, VERDICT_NOTE, 100 * cutoffs_1pct[[1]], 100 * cutoffs_1pct[[2]]))
tails_1pct %>%
  mutate(tail = ifelse(country_year(tails_1pct) %in%
                         country_year(main$all[main$all[[OUTCOME]] < 0, ]), "low", "high"),
         status = ifelse(weather == "yes", "weather", "not weather")) %>%
  count(category, status, tail) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tail, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(status, desc(low + high)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "The 1% tails of growth by likely cause")

# 2. Effects for a typical unit of each third of income (main sample).
typical <- distinct(tail_fits[[1]]$d, GID_1, inc_level, clim_TM, clim_RR) %>%
  mutate(third = factor(c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")[dplyr::ntile(inc_level, 3)],
                        levels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third"))) %>%
  group_by(third) %>%
  summarise(level = mean(inc_level), clim_TM = mean(clim_TM), clim_RR = mean(clim_RR),
            .groups = "drop")
tail_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(tail_fits), function(s) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    bind_rows(lapply(EFFECT_AT, function(x) {
      spline_effect(tail_fits[[s]], v, x, typical[[paste0("clim_", v)]], typical$level) %>%
        mutate(sample = s, variable = v, deviation = x, third = typical$third,
               p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
    }))
  }))
}))
tail_effects$cell <- effect_cell(tail_effects)
tail_effects %>%
  mutate(event = factor(sprintf("%s %+d SD", ifelse(variable == "TM", "T", "P"), deviation),
                        levels = c("T -3 SD", "T +3 SD", "P -3 SD", "P +3 SD")),
         sample = factor(sample, levels = names(TAIL_SAMPLES))) %>%
  arrange(event, third, sample) %>%
  select(event, third, sample, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Splines in climate and income: effect (pp, 95%% CI) of a year at +/-3 SD for a typical unit",
    "of each third of income of the main sample (GDP per capita %s; long-run T %s °C, P %s m)",
    "in each sample; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"),
    paste(format(round(exp(typical$level)), big.mark = ","), collapse = ", "),
    paste(round(typical$clim_TM, 1), collapse = ", "), paste(round(typical$clim_RR, 2), collapse = ", ")))

# 3. Figure: across income at the main sample's average climate.
levels_grid <- seq(min(main_rows$inc_level), max(main_rows$inc_level), length.out = 60)
avg_clim <- c(TM = mean(tail_fits[[1]]$d$clim_TM), RR = mean(tail_fits[[1]]$d$clim_RR))
TAIL_COLOURS <- stats::setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#7f7f7f"), names(TAIL_SAMPLES))
bind_rows(lapply(names(tail_fits), function(s) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    bind_rows(lapply(EFFECT_AT, function(x) {
      spline_effect(tail_fits[[s]], v, x, rep(avg_clim[[v]], length(levels_grid)), levels_grid) %>%
        mutate(sample = s, gdp_pc = exp(levels_grid),
               event = sprintf("%s %+d SD", ifelse(v == "TM", "T", "P"), x))
    }))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(event = factor(event, levels = c("T -3 SD", "T +3 SD", "P -3 SD", "P +3 SD")),
         sample = factor(sample, levels = names(TAIL_SAMPLES))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(gdp_pc, 100 * estimate, colour = sample, fill = sample)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * conf_low, ymax = 100 * conf_high), alpha = 0.1, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~event, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = TAIL_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TAIL_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Long-run GDP per capita (log scale)", y = "Effect on growth of GDP per capita (pp)",
       title = "Splines in climate and income: growth outliers dropped",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste("%s, linear arms, horizon deviations; at the average long-run",
                                "climate (%.1f °C, %.2f m); bands: 95%% CI"),
                          main$label, avg_clim[["TM"]], avg_clim[["RR"]])) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

export_spline_model(tail_fits[["1% tails dropped"]]$spline, tail_fits[["1% tails dropped"]]$d,
                    tail_fits[["1% tails dropped"]]$knots, paste0(SPLINE_STEM, "_tails1pct"),
                    sprintf(paste("the 1%% lowest and 1%% highest growth rates of PWT x ERA5 from the",
                                  "start year (below %.2f%% or above %.2f%%) dropped, whatever their cause"),
                            100 * cutoffs_1pct[[1]], 100 * cutoffs_1pct[[2]]))
```

# Forms and definitions on every panel

The model with income and climate interactions, for each definition (horizon,
20-year, 30-year) and form (symmetric, linear, quadratic and cubic arms), on
each panel. Income is the `r if (params$income_baseline == "horizon") "horizon mean (as in the main notebook)" else "mean of the 20 years before, with its level"`
(the parameter `income_baseline`; see the check above). Within a panel the 12
models are on the same rows: those of the main notebook that also have the
30-year moments (with ERA5, which starts in 1940, the 30-year baseline exists
from 1970, so none are lost; the demeaning of the 30-year deviations is fitted
from 1970 rather than 1960 there).

A cubic arm at 3 SD is 27 times its coefficient. The cubic and quadratic
effects at +/-3 SD therefore rest on the few years that far out, so their
intervals are wide.

The tables:

1. the rows of each panel, and the GDP per capita of the thirds of its units by
   income;
2. for each panel, the fit of the 12 models: within adjusted R2, AIC and BIC
   relative to the best of the panel, each model's verdict against the best of
   the panel and against the best form of its definition, and the joint tests
   of each variable's deviation terms, of its income interactions and of its
   climate interactions;
3. the model each criterion picks on each panel, and how many models cannot be
   told apart from it;
4. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate, at the panel's
   average income;
5. the effects at the mean income of the poorest and of the richest third of
   the units, at the middle climates (15 °C, 1.5 m).

```{r sensitivity}
INCOME_BASELINE <- params$income_baseline
stopifnot(INCOME_BASELINE %in% c("horizon", "lag_20"))
SENS_MOMENTS <- c("mean_TM_lag_30", "sd_TM_lag_30", "mean_RR_lag_30", "sd_RR_lag_30",
                  "dm_TM_lag_30", "dm_RR_lag_30")
# The rows of panel p with the 30-year moments (positive SDs) and its income:
# inc_level (log), inc (centred on the rows).
sens_rows <- function(p) {
  d <- p$clean
  keep <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(SENS_MOMENTS, function(x) is.finite(d[[x]]))) &
    d$sd_TM_lag_30 > 0 & d$sd_RR_lag_30 > 0
  d <- add_income(p, d[keep, ])
  if (INCOME_BASELINE == "lag_20") {
    d <- d %>%
      select(-inc_level, -inc) %>%
      left_join(trailing_income(p$econ), by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
      rename(inc_level = inc_trailing_level) %>%
      filter(is.finite(inc_level))
    d$inc <- d$inc_level - mean(d$inc_level)
  }
  d
}
# Deviations (SD) of the response curves of the figures.
CURVE_X <- seq(-3, 3, by = 0.1)
sens_terms <- function(form) {
  c(form_terms(form), income_interactions(form), if (INCOME_BASELINE == "lag_20") "inc")
}

sens_results <- lapply(names(sens_panels), function(label) {
  p <- sens_panels[[label]]
  d0 <- sens_rows(p)
  # Income of the units' thirds (the units' mean log income), centred.
  units <- d0 %>% group_by(GID_1) %>% summarise(inc_level = mean(inc_level), .groups = "drop")
  third <- dplyr::ntile(units$inc_level, 3)
  centre <- mean(d0$inc_level)
  income_at <- list("average income" = 0,
                    "poorest third" = mean(units$inc_level[third == 1]) - centre,
                    "richest third" = mean(units$inc_level[third == 3]) - centre)
  grid <- expand.grid(form = names(FORMS), definition = names(DEFINITIONS), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  models <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
    d <- add_deviation_terms(d0, DEFINITIONS[[grid$definition[i]]])
    fit_model(sens_terms(FORMS[[grid$form[i]]]), d)
  })
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  records <- lapply(models, fit_record)
  by_definition <- unlist(lapply(names(DEFINITIONS), function(def) {
    k <- which(grid$definition == def)
    stats::setNames(set_verdicts(records[k]), k)
  }))[as.character(seq_len(nrow(grid)))]
  fit <- tibble::tibble(
    panel = label, definition = grid$definition, form = grid$form,
    within_adj_r2 = vapply(records, `[[`, 0, "war2"),
    aic = vapply(records, `[[`, 0, "aic"), bic = vapply(records, `[[`, 0, "bic"),
    vs_best_of_panel = set_verdicts(records), vs_best_form = by_definition,
    T_p = vapply(models, wald_p, 0, dev_pattern("TM")),
    P_p = vapply(models, wald_p, 0, dev_pattern("RR")),
    T_income_p = vapply(models, wald_p, 0, income_pattern("TM")),
    P_income_p = vapply(models, wald_p, 0, income_pattern("RR")),
    T_climate_p = vapply(models, wald_p, 0, climate_pattern("TM")),
    P_climate_p = vapply(models, wald_p, 0, climate_pattern("RR"))
  )
  effects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(income_at), function(k) {
      effects_at(models[[i]], FORMS[[grid$form[i]]], list(inc = income_at[[k]])) %>%
        mutate(panel = label, definition = grid$definition[i], form = grid$form[i], income = k)
    }))
  }))
  # Response curves at the average income, for the figures.
  curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
    m <- models[[i]]
    terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
    bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
      g <- expand.grid(x = CURVE_X, level = seq_along(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]))
      G <- t(mapply(function(x, l) {
        mods <- c(stats::setNames(list(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]][[l]]), paste0("clim_", v)), list(inc = 0))
        deviation_weights(terms, FORMS[[grid$form[i]]][[v]], v, x, mods)
      }, g$x, g$level))
      colnames(G) <- terms
      linear_combination(m, G) %>%
        mutate(variable = v, x = g$x, level = EVAL_LABELS[[v]][g$level])
    })) %>%
      mutate(panel = label, definition = grid$definition[i], form = grid$form[i])
  }))
  sample <- tibble::tibble(
    panel = label, observations = nrow(d0), main_rows = nrow(p$clean),
    countries = n_distinct(d0$GID_0), years = paste(range(d0$year), collapse = "-"),
    gdp_pc_poorest_third = round(exp(mean(units$inc_level[third == 1]))),
    gdp_pc_middle_third = round(exp(mean(units$inc_level[third == 2]))),
    gdp_pc_richest_third = round(exp(mean(units$inc_level[third == 3])))
  )
  # The models are not kept (cache size); only the results above.
  list(sample = sample, fit = fit, effects = effects, curves = curves)
})
```

```{r sensitivity-tables}
sens_fit <- bind_rows(lapply(sens_results, `[[`, "fit"))
sens_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(sens_results, `[[`, "effects"))
sens_effects$column <- effect_column(sens_effects)
sens_effects$cell <- sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * sens_effects$estimate, stars(sens_effects$p_value))
model_label <- function(definition, form) paste0(definition, ", ", form)

# 1. The rows.
bind_rows(lapply(sens_results, `[[`, "sample")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "The rows of each panel (with the 30-year moments; main_rows: the rows of the main",
    "notebook) and the GDP per capita (geometric mean) of the thirds of its units by income"))

# 2. Fit and tests, one table per panel.
for (label in names(sens_panels)) {
  print(knitr::kable(
    filter(sens_fit, panel == label) %>%
      mutate(aic = round(aic - min(aic), 1), bic = round(bic - min(bic), 1),
             within_adj_r2 = round(within_adj_r2, 5),
             across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
      select(-panel),
    caption = paste0(
      label, ": fit of each definition and form (AIC and BIC relative to the best of the panel), ",
      "the verdict of each model against the best of the panel and against the best form of its ",
      "definition (", VERDICT_NOTE, "), and the joint Wald tests (p) of each variable's ",
      "deviation terms, income interactions and climate interactions")))
}

# 3. The model each criterion picks, and the models within noise of it.
bind_rows(lapply(names(sens_panels), function(label) {
  f <- filter(sens_fit, panel == label)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(CRITERIA), function(j) {
    verdict <- vapply(strsplit(f$vs_best_of_panel, " / "), `[[`, "", j)
    tibble::tibble(panel = label, criterion = CRITERIA[[j]],
                   best = model_label(f$definition, f$form)[verdict == "best"],
                   indifferent = sum(verdict == "indifferent"),
                   indifferent_forms = paste(sort(unique(f$form[verdict == "indifferent"])),
                                             collapse = ", "))
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "The model each criterion picks on each panel, among the 12 (3 definitions x 4 forms), the",
    "number of the others that cannot be told apart from it, and their forms"))

# 4. Effects at the average income, one table per panel.
for (label in names(sens_panels)) {
  e <- filter(sens_effects, panel == label, income == "average income")
  print(knitr::kable(
    e %>%
      mutate(column = factor(column, levels = unique(column)),
             model = model_label(definition, form)) %>%
      select(model, column, cell) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell),
    caption = paste0(label, ": effect (pp) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate, at the ",
                     "average income; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1")))
}

# 5. Effects at the poorest and the richest third's income, middle climates.
for (label in names(sens_panels)) {
  e <- filter(sens_effects, panel == label, income != "average income",
              level %in% c("15 °C", "1.5 m"))
  print(knitr::kable(
    e %>%
      mutate(column = factor(paste0(column, ", ", income),
                             levels = unique(paste0(column, ", ", income))),
             model = model_label(definition, form)) %>%
      select(model, column, cell) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell),
    caption = paste0(label, ": effect (pp) of a year at +/-3 SD at 15 °C and 1.5 m, at the mean ",
                     "income of the poorest and of the richest third of the units; ",
                     "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1")))
}
```

The figures show the response of growth to a deviation from -3 to +3 SD at the
average income, one figure per variable and definition. Rows are panels,
columns are long-run climates, and the colours are the four forms. The bands
are 95% CIs (clustered by country).

```{r sensitivity-figures, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 13}
FORM_COLOURS <- c("Symmetric" = "#7f7f7f", "Linear arms" = "#2a78d6",

sens_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(sens_results, `[[`, "curves")) %>%

for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (def in names(DEFINITIONS)) {
  cv <- filter(sens_curves, variable == v, definition == def) %>%

         y = "Effect on growth of GDP per capita (pp)",

                       "deviations"),
         subtitle = paste("At the average income; columns: long-run climate; bands: 95% CI,",
```

# Temperature with income only

Once income is in the model, the climate interactions of the temperature arms
are jointly insignificant on `r main$label`, as on most panels above. Hot
countries are poor, so income takes over the gradient. Here the temperature
arms are interacted with income only, or with the climate only, and compared
with the model that has both. Precipitation keeps both interactions
throughout (horizon deviations, linear arms):

```text
both          dT_a x (c_a + b_a clim_T + h_a inc)
income only   dT_a x (c_a + h_a inc)                  b_a = 0
climate only  dT_a x (c_a + b_a clim_T)               h_a = 0
```

Each restricted model is nested in the one with both, so its verdict uses the
Wald test of the two terms it drops. On every panel (same rows):

1. the fit and the tests, and the coefficients on `r main$label`;
2. the effect of a +/-3 SD temperature year for a typical unit of each third
   of income: the mean income and the mean long-run temperature of the third's
   units (the model with income only does not use the temperature);
3. figure: the effect of a +/-3 SD year across income on `r main$label`. The
   models with the climate are evaluated at the average long-run temperature
   of the rows. The ticks are the units.

```{r temperature-income-only, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
T_ONLY_FORM <- FORMS[["Linear arms"]]
T_ONLY_MODELS <- list("both" = c("clim_TM", "inc"), "income only" = "inc",
                      "climate only" = "clim_TM")
# Terms with the temperature arms interacted with `t_modifiers`; precipitation
# with its climate and income.
t_only_terms <- function(t_modifiers) {
  t_arms <- paste0("devTM", T_ONLY_FORM$TM)
  p_arms <- paste0("devRR", T_ONLY_FORM$RR)
  c(t_arms, as.vector(outer(t_arms, paste0(":", t_modifiers), paste0)),
    p_arms, paste0(p_arms, ":clim_RR"), paste0(p_arms, ":inc"), CONTROLS)
}
# Effects (linear_combination) of a temperature deviation x in model m (of
# T_ONLY_MODELS[[k]]) at the long-run temperatures `clim` and centred incomes
# `inc` (vectors of the same length).
t_only_effect <- function(m, k, x, clim, inc) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  G <- t(vapply(seq_along(clim), function(i) {
    mods <- list(clim_TM = clim[[i]], inc = inc[[i]])[T_ONLY_MODELS[[k]]]
    deviation_weights(terms, T_ONLY_FORM$TM, "TM", x, mods)
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(m, G)
}

t_only <- lapply(stats::setNames(nm = names(sens_panels)), function(label) {
  p <- sens_panels[[label]]
  d <- add_income(p, add_deviation_terms(p$clean, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]]))
  fits <- lapply(T_ONLY_MODELS, function(z) fit_model(t_only_terms(z), d))
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  centre <- mean(d$inc_level)
  units <- distinct(d, GID_1, inc, clim_TM) %>%
    mutate(gdp_pc = exp(inc + centre),
           third = factor(c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")[dplyr::ntile(inc, 3)],
                          levels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")))
  thirds <- units %>%
    group_by(third) %>%
    summarise(units = n(), gdp_pc = round(exp(mean(inc) + centre)),
              mean_T = mean(clim_TM), inc = mean(inc), .groups = "drop")
  tests <- bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(k) {
    m <- fits[[k]]
    dropped_p <- if (k != "both") added_terms_p(fits$both, m)
    tibble::tibble(
      panel = label, model = k, observations = stats::nobs(m),
      within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
      aic_vs_both = round(stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(fits$both), 1),
      dropped_terms_p = if (is.null(dropped_p)) NA_real_ else signif(dropped_p, 2),
      verdict_vs_both = if (is.null(dropped_p)) "" else fit_verdicts(m, fits$both, nested_p = dropped_p),
      T_p = signif(wald_p(m, dev_pattern("TM")), 2),
      T_income_p = if ("inc" %in% T_ONLY_MODELS[[k]]) signif(wald_p(m, income_pattern("TM")), 2) else NA_real_,
      T_climate_p = if ("clim_TM" %in% T_ONLY_MODELS[[k]]) {
        signif(wald_p(m, climate_pattern("TM")), 2)
      } else NA_real_
    )
  }))
  effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(k) {
    bind_rows(lapply(EFFECT_AT, function(x) {
      t_only_effect(fits[[k]], k, x, thirds$mean_T, thirds$inc) %>%
        mutate(panel = label, model = k, deviation = x, third = thirds$third,
               p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
    }))
  }))
  # Curves across income at the average long-run temperature of the rows (main
  # panel only).
  curves <- NULL
  if (label == main$label) {
    grid <- seq(min(units$inc), max(units$inc), length.out = 60)
    curves <- bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(k) {
      bind_rows(lapply(EFFECT_AT, function(x) {
        t_only_effect(fits[[k]], k, x, rep(mean(d$clim_TM), length(grid)), grid) %>%
          mutate(model = k, deviation = x, gdp_pc = exp(grid + centre))
      }))
    }))
  }
  list(tests = tests, effects = effects, thirds = mutate(thirds, panel = label, .before = 1),
       curves = curves, units = units, fits = if (label == main$label) fits)
})

# 1. Fit and tests.
bind_rows(lapply(t_only, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Temperature arms interacted with both, income only or the climate only (precipitation with ",
    "both): within adjusted R2 (%), AIC against both, the Wald test (p) of the two terms dropped ",
    "and the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against both; joint tests (p) of all the temperature terms, of ",
    "their income interactions and of their climate interactions"))
etable(unname(t_only[[main$label]]$fits), headers = names(T_ONLY_MODELS), dict = DICT,
       drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = paste0(main$label, ", linear arms, horizon deviations"))

# 2. Effects for a typical unit of each third of income.
bind_rows(lapply(t_only, `[[`, "thirds")) %>%
  transmute(panel, third, units, gdp_pc, mean_T = round(mean_T, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("The thirds of the units by income: GDP per capita (geometric",
                               "mean) and mean long-run temperature"))
t_only_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(t_only, `[[`, "effects"))
t_only_effects$cell <- effect_cell(t_only_effects)
t_only_effects$column <- factor(
  sprintf("T %+d SD, %s", t_only_effects$deviation, t_only_effects$model),
  levels = as.vector(t(outer(sprintf("T %+d SD", EFFECT_AT), names(T_ONLY_MODELS), paste, sep = ", "))))
t_only_effects %>%
  select(panel, third, column, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Effect (pp, 95% CI) of a temperature year at +/-3 SD for a typical unit of each third of",
    "income (its mean income and mean long-run temperature); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. Figure.
T_ONLY_COLOURS <- c("both" = "#2a78d6", "income only" = "#eb6834", "climate only" = "#7f7f7f")
t_only[[main$label]]$curves %>%
  mutate(event = factor(sprintf("T %+d SD", deviation), levels = sprintf("T %+d SD", EFFECT_AT)),
         model = factor(model, levels = names(T_ONLY_MODELS))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(gdp_pc, 100 * estimate, colour = model, fill = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * conf_low, ymax = 100 * conf_high), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_rug(data = t_only[[main$label]]$units, aes(x = gdp_pc), inherit.aes = FALSE,
           colour = "grey40", alpha = 0.5, sides = "b") +
  facet_wrap(~event) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = T_ONLY_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = T_ONLY_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Long-run GDP per capita (log scale)", y = "Effect on growth of GDP per capita (pp)",
       title = "Temperature response across income",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", linear arms, horizon deviations; the models with the ",
                         "climate at the rows' average long-run temperature; bands: 95% CI; ",
                         "ticks: the units")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

# Oil prices and oil producers

In the model with income, a hot year raises the growth of the richest
countries. At the top of the income range the effect is significant, and most
of the countries there are oil exporters (Qatar, the United Arab Emirates,
Brunei, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait). Does the oil price account for it?

**Data.**
- The oil price is the Energy Institute's crude oil price since 1861, in
  constant 2025 US$ (per cubic metre; the unit drops out in logs). It is from
  the Statistical Review of World Energy 2026, as published by Our World in
  Data (`data/oil/oil-prices-inflation-adjusted.csv`).
- A country's oil production is its oil rents as a share of GDP (WDI
  `NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS`, % of GDP, 1970-2021; `data/oil/wb_oil_rents.csv`). The
  share is averaged over the country's years from `r params$start_year`. It is
  one number per country, so it does not respond to the price of the year.
- A producer is a country whose average share exceeds 10% of GDP.

**Specification.** The oil price is the same for every country in a year, so
the year effects absorb it, and it cannot enter on its own. What can enter is
its interaction with how much a country produces. The model with income
(horizon deviations, linear arms) gets, in turn:

```text
level      h1 log P(t) x share
change     h1 dlog P(t) x share + h2 dlog P(t-1) x share          dlog P(t) = log P(t) - log P(t-1)
dummy      h1 dlog P(t) x producer + h2 dlog P(t-1) x producer
dropped    no oil terms, without the producers
```

All the models are on the rows of `r main$label` whose country has oil rents
in WDI. The baseline is the model without oil terms on the same rows. Each
model with oil terms is nested in it (the Wald test of the oil terms). The
tables:

1. the producers in the sample, and the oil share of the richest countries;
2. the coefficients;
3. the tests: the oil terms, the income interactions of each variable, and
   each model against the baseline;
4. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate. They are evaluated
   at the mean income of the poorest and of the richest third of the units,
   and at the highest income of the sample.

```{r oil-prices}
OIL_PRODUCER_SHARE <- 10
oil_price_raw <- utils::read.csv(data_file("oil/oil-prices-inflation-adjusted.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(names(oil_price_raw)[1:3], c("Entity", "Code", "Year")))
oil_price <- tibble::tibble(year = oil_price_raw$Year, price = oil_price_raw[[4]]) %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(log_oil = log(price),
         dlog_oil = log_oil - lag_by_year(log_oil, year),
         dlog_oil_l1 = lag_by_year(dlog_oil, year))
# Each country's mean oil rents (% of GDP) over its WDI years from the start
# year (no year filled).
oil_share <- read_wdi_csv(data_file("oil/wb_oil_rents.csv"), c(oil_rents = "NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS")) %>%
  filter(year >= START_YEAR, !is.na(oil_rents)) %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(oil_share = mean(oil_rents), oil_years = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(producer = as.numeric(oil_share > OIL_PRODUCER_SHARE))
oil_rows <- check_all %>%
  inner_join(oil_share, by = "GID_0") %>%
  left_join(select(oil_price, year, log_oil, dlog_oil, dlog_oil_l1), by = "year")
stopifnot(!anyNA(oil_rows[, c("log_oil", "dlog_oil", "dlog_oil_l1")]))
OIL_MODELS <- list(
  "baseline" = list(terms = check_terms, rows = oil_rows),
  "level x share" = list(terms = c(check_terms, "log_oil:oil_share"), rows = oil_rows),
  "change x share" = list(terms = c(check_terms, "dlog_oil:oil_share", "dlog_oil_l1:oil_share"),
                          rows = oil_rows),
  "change x producer" = list(terms = c(check_terms, "dlog_oil:producer", "dlog_oil_l1:producer"),
                             rows = oil_rows),
  "producers dropped" = list(terms = check_terms, rows = filter(oil_rows, producer == 0))
)
oil_fits <- lapply(OIL_MODELS, function(m) fit_model(m$terms, m$rows))

# 1. The producers, and the oil share of the richest countries.
oil_units <- distinct(oil_rows, GID_0, inc_level, oil_share, producer, clim_TM)
tibble::tibble(
  sample = c("all", "producers"),
  countries = c(nrow(oil_units), sum(oil_units$producer)),
  rows = c(nrow(oil_rows), sum(oil_rows$producer)),
  missing_oil_rents = c(n_distinct(check_all$GID_0) - nrow(oil_units), NA)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s: the countries with WDI oil rents (missing: countries of the main sample without them, left",
    "out), and the producers (mean oil rents above %d%% of GDP): %s"),
    main$label, OIL_PRODUCER_SHARE,
    paste(sort(oil_units$GID_0[oil_units$producer == 1]), collapse = ", ")))
oil_units %>%
  arrange(desc(inc_level)) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  transmute(GID_0, gdp_pc = round(exp(inc_level)), oil_share = round(oil_share, 1),
            producer = producer == 1, mean_T = round(clim_TM, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("The 15 richest countries: GDP per capita (horizon mean), mean oil",
                               "rents (% of GDP) and long-run temperature (C)"))

# 2. Coefficients.
etable(unname(oil_fits), headers = names(oil_fits),
       dict = c(DICT, "log_oil:oil_share" = "log P x share", "dlog_oil:oil_share" = "dlog P x share",
                "dlog_oil_l1:oil_share" = "dlog P(t-1) x share", "dlog_oil:producer" = "dlog P x producer",
                "dlog_oil_l1:producer" = "dlog P(t-1) x producer",
                # fixest may name an interaction with its parts in the other order.
                "oil_share:dlog_oil_l1" = "dlog P(t-1) x share",
                "producer:dlog_oil_l1" = "dlog P(t-1) x producer"),
       drop = DROP, order = c(ORDER, "oil"), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = paste0(main$label, ", linear arms, horizon deviations, with income; oil share in % of GDP"))

# 3. Tests.
bind_rows(lapply(names(oil_fits), function(k) {
  m <- oil_fits[[k]]
  oil_p <- if (k %in% c("baseline", "producers dropped")) NULL else added_terms_p(m, oil_fits$baseline)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = k, observations = stats::nobs(m),
    within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
    oil_terms_p = if (is.null(oil_p)) NA_real_ else signif(oil_p, 2),
    verdict_vs_baseline = if (is.null(oil_p)) "" else fit_verdicts(m, oil_fits$baseline, nested_p = oil_p),
    T_income_p = signif(wald_p(m, income_pattern("TM")), 2),
    P_income_p = signif(wald_p(m, income_pattern("RR")), 2),
    T_p = signif(wald_p(m, dev_pattern("TM")), 2), P_p = signif(wald_p(m, dev_pattern("RR")), 2)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": within adjusted R2 (%), the Wald test (p) of the oil terms and the ", VERDICT_NOTE,
    " against the baseline (nested, same rows; not for the model without the producers, on other ",
    "rows); joint tests (p) of each variable's income interactions and of all its deviation terms"))

# 4. Effects at three incomes (the units of the oil rows).
oil_third <- dplyr::ntile(oil_units$inc_level, 3)
OIL_INCOME <- c("poorest third" = mean(oil_units$inc_level[oil_third == 1]),
                "richest third" = mean(oil_units$inc_level[oil_third == 3]),
                "highest income" = max(oil_units$inc_level))
oil_centre <- mean(check_all$inc_level)
oil_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(oil_fits), function(k) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(OIL_INCOME), function(lvl) {
    effects_at(oil_fits[[k]], CHECK_FORM, list(inc = OIL_INCOME[[lvl]] - oil_centre)) %>%
      mutate(model = k, income = lvl)
  }))
}))
oil_effects$cell <- effect_cell(oil_effects)
oil_effects %>%
  mutate(event = effect_column(oil_effects),
         income = factor(income, levels = names(OIL_INCOME)),
         model = factor(model, levels = names(OIL_MODELS))) %>%
  select(event, income, model, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell) %>%
  arrange(factor(event, levels = unique(effect_column(oil_effects))), income) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s: effect (pp, 95%% CI) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate, at the mean income of",
    "the poorest and of the richest third of the units and at the highest income (GDP per capita",
    "%s), with and without the oil terms; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"),
    main$label, paste(format(round(exp(OIL_INCOME)), big.mark = ","), collapse = ", ")))
```
